books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.source: Standard Ebooks (미국 퍼블릭 도메인, CC0 편집본)

words.ex: I've been turning his offer over in my mind all week.
words.exKo: 그의 제안을 일주일 내내 곰곰이 되새기고 있다.

cloze.s: I couldn't sleep; I kept ___.
a: turning it over in my mind

cloze.s: She ___ for days before she finally said yes.
a: turned it over in her mind
turned the offer over in her mind

vs.s: He ___ the idea over in his mind before making a decision.
vs.why: turn over in one's mind: 곰곰이 되새기다 / take over: 인계받다 / give over: 넘겨주다

words.note: 소설의 첫 문장에 나와요. think about보다 오래, 여러 번 되짚는 느낌이에요.

words.ex: Only a few managers were privy to the merger plans.
words.exKo: 합병 계획을 아는 사람은 관리자 몇 명뿐이었다.

cloze.s: Only the CEO was ___ the details of the deal.
I wasn't ___ their private conversation.

vs.s: Only two engineers were ___ to the new design.
vs.why: privy to: 비밀을 알고 있는 / private: 사적인 / prior to: ~보다 앞서

words.note: 격식 있는 말이라 비즈니스 이메일에서도 자주 보여요.

words.ex: I'm inclined to agree with you on this one.
words.exKo: 이번 건은 네 말에 동의하는 쪽이야.

cloze.s: After hearing both sides, I'm ___ believe her.
He's ___ overthink small decisions.

vs.s: I'm ___ to think the project will be delayed.
vs.why: be inclined to: ~하는 쪽으로 마음이 기울다 / be included: 포함되다 / decline to: 거절하다

words.note: 의견을 부드럽게 말할 때 좋아요. I'm inclined to think…는 I think…보다 단정하지 않게 들려요.

words.ex: Let's reserve judgment until we see the final results.
words.exKo: 최종 결과를 볼 때까지 판단을 보류하자.

cloze.s: I'll ___ until I've heard his side of the story.
Good managers ___ instead of jumping to conclusions.

vs.s: Don't ___ to conclusions; let's wait for the data.
vs.why: jump to conclusions: 성급히 결론 내리다 / reserve judgment: 판단을 보류하다 / hold off: 미루다

words.note: 원문은 영국식 철자 judgement예요. 미국식은 judgment.

words.ex: She gave me a supercilious smile and walked away.
words.exKo: 그녀는 나를 깔보는 듯한 미소를 짓고 가 버렸다.

cloze.s: His ___ attitude made everyone at the meeting uncomfortable.
The waiter looked at our shoes with a ___ expression.

vs.s: He wasn't just confident; he was ___, treating everyone as beneath him.
vs.why: supercilious: 거만하게 깔보는 / superstitious: 미신을 믿는 / superficial: 피상적인

words.note: 톰 뷰캐넌을 묘사하는 단어예요.

words.ex: The town felt desolate after the factory closed.
words.exKo: 공장이 문을 닫은 뒤 마을은 황량하게 느껴졌다.

cloze.s: We drove through a ___ stretch of desert for hours.
After everyone left, the office looked cold and ___.

vs.s: The abandoned station looked completely ___.
vs.why: desolate: 황량한, 쓸쓸한 / desperate: 절박한 / dedicated: 헌신적인

words.ex: There was a perceptible change in his tone.
words.exKo: 그의 말투에 눈에 띄는 변화가 있었다.

cloze.s: The difference in sound quality is barely ___.
There was a ___ drop in sales after the price increase.

vs.s: The change was so small that it was barely ___.
vs.why: perceptible: (사물이) 감지될 수 있는 / perceptive: (사람이) 눈치 빠른 / permissible: 허용되는

words.ex: Her vitality filled the whole room.
words.exKo: 그녀의 활력이 방 전체를 채웠다.

cloze.s: Regular exercise gave him a new sense of ___.
The city lost its ___ after the main factory closed.

vs.s: Despite her age, she was full of ___ and humor.
vs.why: vitality: 활력 / validity: 타당성, 유효성 / vanity: 허영심

words.ex: Her bold proposal raised a few eyebrows in the meeting.
words.exKo: 그녀의 대담한 제안에 회의에서 몇몇이 눈썹을 치켜올렸다.

cloze.s: When I said I was quitting, my boss ___.
The CEO's strange comment ___ among investors.

vs.s: His decision to skip the meeting ___ a few eyebrows.
vs.why: raise eyebrows: 의아하게 만들다 (타동사 raise) / rise: 스스로 오르다 (목적어 없음) / arise: 생기다

words.note: raise a few eyebrows는 '사람들을 의아하게 만들다'라는 뜻으로 비즈니스 기사에 자주 나와요.

words.ex: He threw up his hands in despair.
words.exKo: 그는 절망해서 두 손을 들었다.

cloze.s: She looked at the broken laptop ___.
After the third rejection, he sat ___ in his car.

vs.s: He shook his head ___ when he saw the test results.
vs.why: in despair: 절망하여 / in charge: 책임을 맡은 / in advance: 미리

words.ex: I felt ill at ease at the formal dinner.
words.exKo: 격식 있는 저녁 자리에서 마음이 편치 않았다.

cloze.s: He seemed ___ among strangers at the party.
New employees often feel ___ for the first few weeks.

vs.s: She felt ___ in the room full of senior executives.
vs.why: ill at ease: 불편한 / at ease: 편안한 / at large: (범인이) 잡히지 않은, 전반적인

words.ex: I came across an old photo while cleaning my room.
words.exKo: 방을 치우다가 옛날 사진을 우연히 발견했다.

cloze.s: I ___ a great article about battery research yesterday.
If you ___ any typos, please let me know.

vs.s: While searching online, I ___ an interesting job posting.
vs.why: come across: 우연히 발견하다 / come up with: (아이디어를) 생각해 내다 / come down with: (병에) 걸리다

words.note: come across as(~라는 인상을 주다)도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

words.ex: The doctor's words gave me some reassurance.
words.exKo: 의사의 말이 나를 좀 안심시켰다.

cloze.s: New team members need a little ___ in their first week.
He looked at me for ___ before he started speaking.

vs.s: Before the exam, her mother's ___ calmed her down.
vs.why: reassurance: 걱정을 덜어 주는 안심 / insurance: 보험 / assurance: 확언, 보증

words.ex: Without a car, you're at a disadvantage in this city.
words.exKo: 이 도시에서는 차가 없으면 불리하다.

cloze.s: Students without internet access ___ during online classes.
I felt ___ because I was the only one who didn't speak French.

vs.s: Without the right data, our team will be at a ___.
vs.why: at a disadvantage: 불리한 / at a discount: 할인된 / at a distance: 멀리서

words.ex: It was careless of me to leave the door unlocked.
words.exKo: 문을 잠그지 않은 건 내 부주의였다.

cloze.s: One ___ mistake ruined the whole report.
He made a ___ remark that hurt her feelings.

vs.s: Leaving your password on a sticky note is really ___.
vs.why: careless: 부주의한 / carefree: 근심 걱정 없는 / caring: 배려심 있는

words.note: 이 소설의 핵심 단어예요. 마지막 장에서 다시 중요하게 나와요.

books.coverCredit: 표지: Francis Cugat, Celestial Eyes (1925 초판 표지화, 퍼블릭 도메인) · Standard Ebooks 표지 디자인 (CC0)

books.title: Siddhartha
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.source: Standard Ebooks (Gunther Olesch 외 번역, 2001년 퍼블릭 도메인 공개 · CC0 편집본)
books.coverCredit: 표지: Abanindranath Tagore, The Victory of Buddha (1914, 퍼블릭 도메인) · Standard Ebooks 표지 디자인 (CC0)

words.ex: As a new intern, she was thirsty for feedback on every report.
words.exKo: 신입 인턴이던 그녀는 보고서마다 피드백을 몹시 갈망했다.

cloze.s: He moved to Seoul, ___ new experiences.
The students were ___ real-world examples, not more theory.

vs.s: Young Siddhartha was ___ for knowledge.
vs.why: thirsty for: ~을 갈망하는 / dry: 마른, 건조한 / empty: 비어 있는

words.note: 물을 마시고 싶은 갈증을 지식·경험 같은 추상적인 것에 빗댄 표현이에요. 이 책 전체에서 thirst(갈증)가 반복되는 핵심 이미지예요.

words.ko: 가장 깊은 곳의, 마음속 깊이 숨겨진
words.ex: She rarely shares her innermost feelings, even with close friends.
words.exKo: 그녀는 친한 친구에게도 마음속 깊은 감정을 거의 털어놓지 않는다.

cloze.s: In his diary he wrote down his ___ fears.
The ___ room of the temple was closed to visitors.

vs.s: He finally told her his ___ thoughts.
vs.why: innermost: 가장 안쪽의, 내밀한 / outermost: 가장 바깥쪽의 / uppermost: 가장 위의, 가장 중요한

words.note: inner(안쪽의)의 최상급처럼 쓰여요. feelings, thoughts, self와 자주 붙어요.

words.ex: I was so lost in thought that I missed my subway stop.
words.exKo: 생각에 너무 잠겨 있어서 지하철역을 지나쳤다.

cloze.s: He stared out the window, ___.
She walked home slowly, completely ___.

vs.s: Siddhartha sat there ___ in thought.
vs.why: lost in thought: 생각에 잠긴 / missed: 놓친 / gone: 사라진

words.note: be lost in ~ 은 어떤 것에 '빠져서' 주변을 잊은 상태예요. lost in a book(책에 빠진)처럼도 써요.

words.ex: Training for a marathon takes months of self-denial.
words.exKo: 마라톤 준비에는 몇 달간의 극기가 필요하다.

cloze.s: The monks lived a life of strict ___.
Saving that much money required a lot of ___.

vs.s: Fasting is a form of ___.
vs.why: self-denial: 극기, 자기 부정 / self-esteem: 자존감 / self-service: 셀프서비스

words.note: Samana(고행자)들이 추구하는 길을 가리키는 말이에요. 2장에서 여러 번 다시 나와요.

words.ex: With your permission, I'd like to record this meeting.
words.exKo: 허락해 주신다면 이 회의를 녹음하고 싶습니다.

cloze.s: ___, I'll leave a little early today.
___, sir, I'd like to ask one more question.

vs.s: ___ your permission, I'd like to share my screen.
vs.why: with your permission: 허락해 주신다면 / by, on은 이 표현에 쓰지 않아요

words.note: 격식 있는 자리에서 무언가를 하기 전에 정중하게 양해를 구할 때 써요. 비즈니스 회의에서도 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.

words.ex: He spoke about his old company with open contempt.
words.exKo: 그는 예전 회사에 대해 대놓고 경멸하듯 말했다.

cloze.s: She looked at the offer with ___.
The manager treated our ideas with ___.

vs.s: His voice was full of ___ for the lazy staff.
vs.why: contempt: 경멸 / content: 내용, 만족한 / context: 맥락

words.note: with contempt(경멸하며), hold ~ in contempt(~을 경멸하다) 형태로 자주 써요.

words.ex: She overcame her fear of public speaking by practising every day.
words.exKo: 그녀는 매일 연습해서 발표 공포증을 극복했다.

cloze.s: We need to ___ a few technical problems before launch.
He finally ___ his shyness and asked her out.

vs.s: It took years to ___ the injury.
vs.why: overcome: 극복하다 / overlook: 간과하다 / overtake: 추월하다

words.note: 과거형 overcame, 과거분사 overcome이에요. be overcome by(감정 등에 압도되다)로도 써요.

words.ex: Scrolling through my phone at night just numbs my brain.
words.exKo: 밤에 휴대폰을 넘겨 보는 건 그냥 머리를 멍하게 만들 뿐이다.

cloze.s: My fingers were ___ from the cold.
He used work to ___ the pain of the breakup.

vs.s: The cold water ___ his feet.
vs.why: numb: 마비시키다 / number: 번호를 매기다 / nod: 끄덕이다

words.note: b는 소리 나지 않아요(넘). 고통이나 감정을 '잠깐 무디게' 하는 뉘앙스로 이 장에서 쓰여요.

words.ex: He's under the delusion that the project will finish itself.
words.exKo: 그는 프로젝트가 저절로 끝날 거라고 착각하고 있다.

cloze.s: She lives under the ___ that everyone likes her.
Thinking we could win without practice was a ___.

vs.s: He was under the ___ that he was always right.
vs.why: delusion: 망상, 착각 / direction: 방향 / decision: 결정

words.note: be under the delusion that ~ (~라고 착각하다) 형태가 가장 흔해요.

words.ex: I'm on my way to the lab now.
words.exKo: 지금 연구실로 가는 중이야.

cloze.s: Don't start without me, I'm ___.
Many travellers were ___ to the city.

vs.s: I'll call you when I'm ___ my way home.
vs.why: on one's way: 가는 중 / in the way: 방해가 되는 / at은 쓰지 않아요

words.note: 책에서는 get on their way(길을 나서다), went on their way(가던 길을 갔다)로 나와요. 문자로는 'On my way!'가 아주 흔해요.

words.ex: I'm not content with a B; I want to retake the exam.
words.exKo: B로는 만족 못 해. 시험 다시 보고 싶어.

cloze.s: She was ___ a small apartment near campus.
Don't be ___ the first draft.

vs.s: He was content ___ a simple life.
vs.why: be content with + 명사 / be content to + 동사원형 (~하는 것으로 만족하다)

words.note: content(만족한)는 형용사일 때 뒤에 강세(컨텐트)예요. 명사 content(내용, 콘텐츠)는 앞에 강세예요.

words.ex: This mistake in no way reflects your ability.
words.exKo: 이 실수가 네 능력을 보여주는 건 결코 아니야.

cloze.s: The new rule is ___ meant to punish anyone.
I am ___ responsible for what happened.

vs.s: This ___ no way changes our plan.
vs.why: in no way: 결코 ~ 아닌 / by no means도 같은 뜻이에요

words.note: not보다 훨씬 강하게 부정해요. 문장 맨 앞에 오면 In no way did he… 처럼 도치돼요.

words.ex: He renounced his inheritance and started his own business.
words.exKo: 그는 상속을 포기하고 자기 사업을 시작했다.

cloze.s: She ___ her old beliefs after the trip.
Monks ___ worldly possessions.

vs.s: He ___ his citizenship to work abroad.
vs.why: renounce: 포기하다 / announce: 발표하다 / pronounce: 발음하다

words.note: give up보다 공식적이고 단호한 느낌이에요. 권리·직위·국적·신념을 공개적으로 버릴 때 써요.

words.ex: I finally summoned my courage and asked the professor for a reference letter.
words.exKo: 마침내 용기를 내서 교수님께 추천서를 부탁드렸다.

cloze.s: She ___ and raised her hand.
It took me a week to ___ to call him.

vs.s: He ___ his courage and spoke to the Buddha.
vs.why: summon one's courage: 용기를 내다 / summon은 '불러 모으다'라서 용기·힘과 어울려요

words.note: summon up the courage to + 동사원형 형태로도 자주 써요.

words.ex: Thank you for your unwavering support this year.
words.exKo: 올해 변함없이 지지해 주셔서 감사합니다.

cloze.s: She showed ___ commitment to the project.
His ___ focus impressed the interviewers.

vs.s: He looked at me with an ___ gaze.
vs.why: unwavering: 흔들림 없는 / unwilling: 내키지 않는 / unaware: 모르는

words.note: waver(흔들리다, 망설이다)의 반대예요. 감사 메일에서 unwavering support로 자주 쓰여요.

words.ex: Our new team lead is sharp-witted and catches mistakes instantly.
words.exKo: 새 팀장은 눈치가 빨라서 실수를 바로 잡아낸다.

cloze.s: The ___ boy found a way out of the trouble.
You need to be ___ to win a debate.

vs.s: Suan was a clever, ___-witted boy.
vs.why: sharp-witted: 머리가 빠른 / dull-witted, slow-witted: 둔한

words.note: sharp(날카로운) + wit(재치). quick-witted도 거의 같은 뜻이에요.

words.ex: I tried to call him all morning, but in vain.
words.exKo: 아침 내내 그에게 전화했지만 소용없었다.

cloze.s: They searched for the key, but ___.
All our efforts were ___.

vs.s: She waited for an answer, but ___ vain.
vs.why: in vain: 헛되이 / 다른 전치사는 쓰지 않아요

words.note: 이야기책에서 '애썼지만 실패했다'를 짧게 말할 때 자주 나와요. 문장 끝에 but in vain으로 붙는 형태가 흔해요.

words.ex: The city called for volunteers to clean up the river.
words.exKo: 시는 강 청소 자원봉사자를 모집했다.

cloze.s: The union ___ higher wages.
This situation ___ quick action.

vs.s: The king ___ for volunteers to find the ring.
vs.why: call for: 공개적으로 요청하다 / ask for: (개인적으로) 부탁하다 / look for: 찾다

words.note: '(상황이) ~을 필요로 하다'라는 뜻도 있어요. This calls for a celebration!(이건 축하할 일이야!)

words.ex: It so happened that my professor was on the same train.
words.exKo: 마침 교수님이 같은 기차에 타고 계셨다.

cloze.s: ___ the store was closed that day.
___ we both chose the same topic.

vs.s: It so ___ that I met her at the airport.
vs.why: it so happened that: 우연히 그렇게 되었다 / appear, seem은 '~처럼 보이다'

words.note: 이야기에서 우연한 사건을 꺼낼 때 쓰는 말이에요. As it happened, …도 같은 뜻이에요.

words.ex: Many young Filipinos move abroad in search of better jobs.
words.exKo: 많은 필리핀 청년들이 더 나은 일자리를 찾아 해외로 간다.

cloze.s: He left home ___ adventure.
They walked from village to village ___ water.

vs.s: They travelled the world ___ search of the truth.
vs.why: in search of: ~을 찾아서 / search for(동사)와 헷갈리지 마세요

words.note: 명사 search 앞에 in을 붙여 '찾는 중'이라는 상태를 나타내요.

words.ex: At last, the results of the experiment came out.
words.exKo: 드디어 실험 결과가 나왔다.

cloze.s: After hours of waiting, the bus ___ arrived.
___ he understood what she meant.

vs.s: We waited for weeks, and ___ last the visa came.
vs.why: at last: 마침내 / finally와 비슷하지만 '오래 기다렸다'는 느낌이 더 강해요

words.note: 기다림이나 고생 끝에 일이 이뤄질 때 써요. 감탄처럼 'At last!'만 따로 쓰기도 해요.

words.ex: The company finally got possession of the building last month.
words.exKo: 그 회사는 지난달 마침내 그 건물을 손에 넣었다.

cloze.s: The thief tried to ___ the map.
She ___ the old house after a long legal fight.

vs.s: The princess played tricks to ___ possession of the purse.
vs.why: get(gain) possession of: 손에 넣다 / take possession of도 쓰지만 '공식적으로 넘겨받다'에 가까워요

words.note: possession(소유)을 써서 '가진 상태가 되다'를 격식 있게 말해요. gain possession of도 같은 뜻이에요.

words.ex: Without a clear plan, the project was doomed to fail.
words.exKo: 명확한 계획 없이 그 프로젝트는 실패할 수밖에 없었다.

cloze.s: They knew the old bridge was ___ collapse.
Without water, the plants were ___ die.

vs.s: Without customers, the shop was ___ to close.
vs.why: doomed to: 나쁜 운명 / destined to: 좋거나 중립적인 운명 / designed to: ~하도록 설계된

words.note: doom은 '파멸, 비운'이에요. destined와 달리 거의 항상 나쁜 결과에 써요.

words.ex: I'll try my best to finish the report by Friday.
words.exKo: 금요일까지 보고서를 끝내도록 최선을 다할게요.

cloze.s: He ___ to pull the horns off, but he couldn't.
Just ___ and don't worry about the result.

vs.s: She ___ her best to stay calm.
vs.why: try/do one's best: 최선을 다하다 / make, take와는 쓰지 않아요

words.note: do one's best와 같은 뜻이에요. try one's best to + 동사원형 형태로 많이 써요.

words.ex: We set out early to avoid the traffic.
words.exKo: 차 막히는 걸 피하려고 일찍 출발했다.

cloze.s: The cook ___ immediately to find a doctor.
They ___ to build a better app.

vs.s: They ___ out on a long journey to the north.
vs.why: set out: 출발하다, 착수하다 / put out: (불을) 끄다 / take out: 꺼내다

words.note: set out to + 동사원형은 '~하려고 작정하다'라는 뜻이에요. 자기소개서에서 I set out to …로 쓰기 좋아요.

words.ex: Semiconductors play an important part in the Korean economy.
words.exKo: 반도체는 한국 경제에서 중요한 역할을 한다.

cloze.s: Teamwork ___ in our success.
Data will ___ in the final decision.

vs.s: Trade played an important ___ in the city's growth.
vs.why: play a part/role: 역할을 하다 / piece, place는 쓰지 않아요

words.note: play an important role in과 같은 뜻이에요. 발표나 보고서에서 아주 자주 써요.

words.ex: The project is more or less finished.
words.exKo: 프로젝트는 거의 끝났다.

cloze.s: The two plans are ___ the same.
I ___ agree with you.

vs.s: The meeting went ___ as planned.
vs.why: more or less: 대체로 / 순서를 바꿔 less or more로 쓰지 않아요

words.note: 정확하진 않지만 대략 맞다는 뜻이에요. 회화에서 '얼추'라는 느낌으로 많이 써요.

words.ex: After the first round, our team was in the lead.
words.exKo: 첫 라운드 뒤 우리 팀이 앞서 있었다.

cloze.s: Japan was far ___ at that time.
Which company is ___ in AI chips?

vs.s: Korea is ___ the lead in memory chips.
vs.why: in the lead: 앞서 있는 / take the lead: 앞장서다

words.note: far in the lead처럼 far로 차이를 강조할 수 있어요.

words.ex: He was excused from the exam by reason of illness.
words.exKo: 그는 병 때문에 시험을 면제받았다.

cloze.s: The event was cancelled ___ bad weather.
She was chosen ___ her experience.

vs.s: Japan led ___ reason of its larger population.
vs.why: by reason of: ~ 때문에 / because of보다 훨씬 격식 있는 말이에요

words.note: 법률·공문서 말투예요. 일상에서는 because of나 due to를 쓰면 돼요.

words.ex: The new design closely resembles last year's model.
words.exKo: 새 디자인은 작년 모델과 아주 비슷하다.

cloze.s: She ___ her mother.
The process ___ a chemical reaction.

vs.s: The two countries ___ each other in many ways.
vs.why: resemble은 타동사라 with, to 없이 바로 목적어가 와요

words.note: resemble with / resemble to는 흔한 실수예요. be similar to와 뜻은 같아요.

words.ex: In the course of the interview, I mentioned my lab project.
words.exKo: 면접 중에 연구실 프로젝트 이야기를 했다.

cloze.s: ___ my research, I found an error in the data.
Prices will rise ___ the next few years.

vs.s: Many things changed ___ the course of the war.
vs.why: in the course of: ~ 동안 / of course(물론)와 헷갈리지 마세요

words.note: during과 비슷하지만 '과정을 거치며'라는 느낌이 더 있어요.

words.ex: The court ruled in our favor.
words.exKo: 법원은 우리에게 유리한 판결을 내렸다.

cloze.s: The odds are ___ this time.
The vote went ___.

vs.s: The new rules work in ___ favor.
vs.why: in + 소유격(my, your, our…) + favor

words.note: 미국식 철자는 favor, 영국식은 favour예요.

words.ex: Good teachers inspire students, who in turn inspire others.
words.exKo: 좋은 선생님은 학생에게 영감을 주고, 그 학생들이 이번엔 다른 사람에게 영감을 준다.

cloze.s: We help our customers, and they ___ recommend us.
Each student spoke ___.

vs.s: Lower costs lead to lower prices, which ___ turn increase sales.
vs.why: in turn: 결과적으로, 이번엔 / by turns: 번갈아

words.note: 원인 → 결과가 이어지는 연쇄를 설명할 때 쓰기 좋아요. 보고서 문장에 유용해요.
